Apple Watch Series 12 will officially go on sale this Friday (click here to pre-order), but some users upgrading may be surprised by a subtle design change that Apple didn't mention at the launch event: the screen bezels have become thicker.

The Apple Watch Series 12 case size has slightly increased to accommodate wider screen bezels

Looking back at the evolution of Apple's product design, it's easy to see that the company's consistent approach has been to narrow the bezels as much as possible.

Over the years, iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch have all progressively narrowed their bezels, making the design more focused on the screen itself.

However, with the Apple Watch Series 12, the direction has reversed—bezels have instead become slightly thicker.

According to Apple's official website, here is a comparison of the case sizes between the Series 12 and the previous two generations:

Series 12 Series 11 Series 10 42mm 42mm by 37mm 42mm by 36mm 42mm by 36mm 46mm 46mm by 40mm 46mm by 39mm 46mm by 39mm

From this, we can see that although the Apple Watch Series 12 has the same case height as the previous generation, its width has slightly increased. However, as seen from this comparison page, the screen sizes of all three models are actually the same.

  • 42mm: 374 x 446 pixels, screen area 970 square millimeters
  • 46mm: 416 x 496 pixels, screen area 1196 square millimeters

In other words, compared to older models, the Apple Watch Series 12's screen is slightly smaller relative to its larger case, making the screen bezels appear more prominent.

The Series 12 features significant internal upgrades, including an all-new health sensing system and the S11 chip, so it's understandable that the case dimensions needed to be adjusted.

However, if you're upgrading from a recent model, be aware that this design choice may give the impression of a step backwards in appearance, as it doesn't follow the consistent trend of narrowing bezels.

What are your thoughts on Apple's decision to enlarge the bezels on the Apple Watch Series 12? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
